meta.foundedNote: 1979 is explicitly reported in Vinay Upasani's Marathi account of 7 September 2011 and printed in Vrittamanas on 5 September 2025. This is stronger than inferring 1979 from a 38 th-festival label in 2016; an original founding record has not yet been located.
meta.intro: Kastur Park's Shree Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal is a neighbourhood festival in Borivali West. Its history brings together housing-society volunteers, social-awareness presentations and elaborate temporary settings. A dated Marathi account explicitly places its beginning in 1979, later repeated in a local newspaper caption. Reports from different years show how the festival's scenery, public messages and organising conditions changed. This collection includes two genuine idol photographs with publication-year evidence and a separate community photograph whose capture date remains unverified.

paragraphs.text: In his 7 September 2011 Marathi account, journalist Vinay Upasani credits Professor Ram Kamat and Chandrakant Kadam with starting the festival in 1979. He describes it as a shared neighbourhood Ganesh supported by housing societies and quotes mandal adviser Sanyog Raje. The 1979 date is also printed beside Kastur Park's photograph in the 5 September 2025 Vrittamanas edition. These published histories support a reported founding date; the first minutes, receipts and photographs remain to be found.

Upasani records organ donation as the 2011 theme, presented through audiovisual material. His account also describes medical camps, student competitions and educational assistance, showing a festival concerned with social issues as well as darshan. The 2018 Times of India plastic-ban report later names Kasturpark among mandals promoting avoidance of plastic. These are documented activities in particular years, not a verified current service programme.

Loksatta's published 2014 competition results name Narendra Bhagat of Kastur Park for the Jogeshwari-to-Dahisar art-direction award. This is a regional category within that competition, not the overall “Mumbaicha Raja” title. The result supplies one named artistic connection without establishing authorship for other years.

Ambarish Mishra's 2016 report describes a Kedarnath-inspired plaster-of-Paris setting lit with traditional brass lamps. Working president Sanyog Raje said volunteers visited Uttarakhand that June to study the shrine. The report calls it the mandal's 38 th year. This documents a temporary architectural environment for Ganesh worship, rather than a permanent Kedarnath temple in Borivali.

The competition organiser's October 2018 announcement lists Kastur Park in the Jogeshwari-to-Dahisar art-direction nominations. It prints the nominee's name as चंद्रकांत शेडके?, including a question mark. This is retained as an unresolved published spelling; the announcement is not evidence that the nominee won, nor enough to identify him with a differently spelled artist elsewhere.

Bella Jaisinghani's 2018 reporting connects redevelopment in Kastur Park with dispersed residents, reduced volunteers, shrinking compound space and lower festival contributions. Sanyog Raje described the difficulty of maintaining a society-based festival when families moved away. This account preserves an important part of mandal history that an idol-only sequence would miss: the social and physical space that makes an annual celebration possible.

sections.title: Transporting the idol and sharing the stage

paragraphs.text: A September 2012 report records Sanyog Raje's concern about bringing the mandal's eight-foot Ganesh from Jogeshwari by truck over damaged roads. This contemporary account preserves part of the annual making and arrival process, but does not name the sculptor. It cannot establish that the same workshop or figure size was used in every subsequent year.

The college's 2019-20 Public Health Office report locates a first-aid awareness camp at Kasturpark Ganesh utsav Mandal. Its event section dates the activity to 11 September 2019 and describes demonstrations presented to an aarti tune, with 14 student participants. The summary table gives a different date, so the precise day remains qualified. This documents how the festival stage was used for public education; historical medical instructions in the report are not reproduced here.

visualReview.observedForm: Crowned four-armed Ganesh seated cross-legged in bright yellow-green trousers, raised blessing hand and two upper implements; carved stone-like pillars, arch, brass standing lamps and hanging lamps in a dark physical mandap.
visualReview.note: Photo opened and inspected. The setting aligns with the contemporaneously reported Kedarnath-inspired pandal. Exact capture day is not supplied by the accessible photo caption.
